title: Finite bit construction: sparse R439 kernel entrance gauge (no new kappa)
body:
## Result and status

**Finite bit frame-word construction plus a scoped sparse-kernel census; no new kappa or hosted supplier admission.**

On the selected PR589 R439 word, a response-kernel basis change lets helper **444 start at frame79** and finish at the full frame: a local residual width of **seven rather than eight**. Helper470 supplies the restored shear. The complete finite scalar map is unchanged on all661 arbitrary input columns.

- Complete local ADDs: **24,305 -> 24,252**, including both new shears and all scatter work.
- Local paid profile: **-H1**, rank mass **5,129 -> 5,128**; nine COPY/ERASE pairs unchanged.
- Exact forward/reverse positive envelopes remain **F=49,347, B=1,113,070**, giving93 local/177 nine-stage bits under inherited104/192 ceilings.
- All compensation-kernel supports of size<=4 are enumerated independently by two methods: **4 pairs,22 triples,54 quadruples**. Exactly one support, **{444,470}**, has a nonzero rational intersection of its first raw contact frames. Both pivot orientations pass.

This is **not a drop-in selected-supplier replacement**. The changed entrance needs its own owner/window and compiler admission. Charging an extra rank-one idle child in the old width-eight host cancels the local -H1 before adapters; no global gain is claimed.

## Novelty and predecessor credit

Kernel entrances are prior work: **Dugongue's PR254** and **Chafik Boukhalfa's PR382** are explicitly credited. This transfers that mechanism to PR589 and adds the complete sparse-kernel/common-frame classification. It changes the fixed-helper-basis hypothesis deliberately excluded by **Ali Romman's PR1128**, rather than contradicting it.

**PR1043/1079 already delete helper470 through source77.** This keeps all439 helpers, establishes a distinct nonzero-entrance boundary witness, and does not claim to beat that construction's bit bound or scalar invoice. DreamingOfClouds, eumemic, Sagar Thakrar, Ali Romman and Hanson Sun retain explicit lineage/method credit. No Adam Gall PR1098 or PR1114 task is repeated.

Only `research/bit-kernel-entrance-seed18/` is added. Base: `c0e3631dc24e3c24a861f7d3d79e0608481cccec`; OS seed18, bit-supplier track. Selected PR1094 and `upstream/` are untouched. Authenticated GitHub had no pinned coordination issue; a local claim and parent scope coordination are recorded. The final overlap scan covered788 open PR bodies and recovered the older kernel-gauge predecessors above.

## Reproduce and exercised evidence

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-kernel-entrance-seed18/verify.py
python3 -I -O -B research/bit-kernel-entrance-seed18/test_package.py
```

Expected verifier marker:

`PASS_BIT_KERNEL_ENTRANCE supports=80 viable=1 columns=661 ADDs=24305->24252 local_mass=5129->5128 controls=6 no_new_kappa`

Completed local verification on Linux/CPython3.14.4:

- Full finite certificate generation; all80 rational intersections and96,141 pair candidates; independent increasing-triple enumeration.
- Baseline and both pivot orientations; full formal-column frame replay and independent literal COPY/ERASE set replay in both scalar directions.
- Six mathematical negative controls, three exhaustive small-matrix subset oracles and two subprocess source-corruption/missing-source controls.
- Complete optimized replay in a minimal offline relocated tree matches the certificate.
- `git diff --cached --check` passes.

The initial180-second attempt timed out before completion. Immutable frame-geometry reuse and zero-factor elimination skips resolved redundant exact arithmetic; the complete final two-command suite passed in113.81seconds. No native5/9/11-stage replay, changed hosting, global invoice, outer assembly, remote CI or full theorem proof is claimed. Exact source hashes, complete certificate, bounded domain, written boundary proof and exercised-check receipt are included.

Prepared by **Adam Gall (@adamgall)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, under Apache-2.0. No independent human review is implied.
